title: What an “income” client really needs
objectives: Find out which of three things an “income” client really wants before recommending an option.
Separate regular cash, the feeling of earning, and habit.
body_md:
Clients who ask for IDCW usually want one of three things: regular cash, a feeling of earning, or habit (“my father always took dividends”). Find out which before recommending an option. Regular cash is a genuine need: the client needs a predictable amount on a predictable date. The feeling of earning is psychological: a payout feels like income even though it is the client's own money coming back. Habit is the hardest: a family tradition of taking “dividends” that survives the 2021 renaming and the 2020 tax change. Each want points to a different answer — and only the first is well served by a payout at all.

- Regular cash → needs a predictable amount on a predictable date
- A feeling of earning → a payout feels like income, though it is own money back
- Habit → “my father always took dividends”; explain what changed in 2020–2021
example: A retiree who needs ₹25,000 on the 5th of every month needs control of amount and date — that points to an SWP, not to a trustee-decided payout.
say: Find out which of the three wants the client really has before recommending.
Habit is not a reason to keep a tax-inefficient option.
never: Every client asking for IDCW wants the same thing.
A payout that feels like income is extra income.

check.q: A client asks for IDCW because “my father always took dividends”. What do you do first?
o: Find out what they really want: regular cash, a feeling of earning, or habit
Explain that dividends no longer exist
check.why: Clients who ask for IDCW usually want one of three things: regular cash, a feeling of earning, or habit. Find out which before recommending an option.

check.q: Which client want is genuinely served by a payout?
o: A desire for the highest NAV
Regular cash on a predictable date — and even then, an SWP usually serves it better
check.why: For regular income, an SWP usually beats IDCW on both control and tax.

check.q: Why did SEBI rename “dividend” to IDCW?
o: The old word misled investors: a payout is not a company dividend paid from profits on top of the investment
check.why: SEBI required the new name from 1 April 2021 because the old word misled investors.
